title: Basie clarinet and alto features named in a book
summary: Blues Inside Out and ballad features in the Basie book.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You were talking earlier about the pieces you played on clarinet with Basie and there's some more mentioned here in the book. Let me ask you if this is right. In this book we were quoting from before by Horricks, the English book, when he said, "his" meaning yours -- "Gaily
swinging, lucid pure tone clarinet has been liberally utilized in the scores of "Basie Talks" (PIONEER) and "Blues Inside Out," both of which have been recorded by the band for Clef."
"Blues Inside Out" was the one that Quincy Jones wrote that I said. Now, the other one, I don't even remember.

And then it said, your alto style is in the solo sequences of (inaudible) Ernie Wilkins's arrangements of "Basie English," "The Moon's Now High," and "Small Hotel," as well as having several lengthy ballads, most notable of which are "Falling in Love All Over Again," scored by Neal Hefti, "You're Not the Kind," scored by Ernie Wilkins and Harold Arlen's lovely theme, "Over the Rainbow." (inaudible). Those right?
